<a id="mission"></a>

## Mission

You build ONE unit: the daemon's EVENT STREAM. Today every interface fs3 has must invent activity, because the daemon tells nobody what it is doing (DL-045) — the render POC inferred progress from poll deltas, the TUI POC faked a feed, and `flowspace3 add` sits silent through an entire walk. You retire that for good: real events at the points work actually completes, served as NDJSON on one endpoint that any number of consumers can read. You report to the PM (pij-near-carp), not to prime.

A new kind or a changed field is a stop-and-ask, because u-t is building against these types RIGHT NOW. |
| u2 | EMIT AT THE DAEMON'S EXISTING LIFECYCLE, invent none: job_done and job_failed beside the runner's own settlement (crates/daemon/src/runner.rs — the serial settle path around complete_job/jobs_remaining, its park/retry/fail branches, and the batched embed path's own completion point); queue after a settlement that changes a depth the daemon already recomputes; root_changed in crates/daemon/src/roots.rs (add/rescan) and crates/daemon/src/remove.rs; heartbeat per subscriber in the stream handler. No second worker loop, no new source of truth about what "done" means. |
| u3 | SCAN PROGRESS is the one genuinely new measurement and it is Jordan's ruling: emit scan_progress DURING the walk that add/scan performs before answering (crates/daemon/src/roots.rs), carrying root, root_path, files_seen, enqueued and the current repo-relative path. ON A CADENCE — time- or count-based — NEVER once per file: a 40,000-file add would otherwise become 40,000 lines no human reads and no TUI can draw. Choose the cadence explicitly, state the number and your reason in your service page, and remember that a default is a number nobody chose. |
| u4 | GET /events serves NDJSON (Content-Type application/x-ndjson), one object per line, flushed per line, never pretty-printed, connection held open until the client hangs up. Accept ?heartbeat_ms to override the cadence. No cursor and no replay: this is a live feed, and a consumer that needs the whole truth asks GET /status, which is a snapshot by design. Add the route beside the existing ones in crates/daemon/src/http.rs. |
| u5 | MULTI-SUBSCRIBER, and the rule that protects indexing: two watchers attached at once receive the SAME events (ac-0004 asserts it with a two-subscriber identity test). Fan out from one in-process broadcast held in AppState. A slow consumer is DROPPED from the fan-out, never allowed to back-pressure the runner — indexing must never wait on a dashboard. A dropped consumer notices at its next heartbeat gap and reconnects. |
| u6 | `flowspace3 status --watch` is yours, and it is your ONLY edit to crates/cli/src/main.rs (the Status arm) plus one `pub mod watch;` line: connect to /events and stream it. In JSON/piped mode print the raw NDJSON lines verbatim, so an agent parses exactly what the daemon sent; in human mode a live summary is welcome but must not be a second renderer — if you want screens, hand the PM a request, do not grow one here. Plain `status` with no --watch must be byte-identical to today; `cargo test -p fs3-cli --test envelope_goldens` is the tripwire and it must stay green. |
| u7 | TESTS THAT PROVE IT OFFLINE: contract tests over the frozen types (round-trip every kind you emit); an emission test per completion point using the daemon's existing harnesses (crates/daemon/tests/support spawns the real router on an ephemeral port; crates/daemon/tests/streaming.rs shows the runner driven against seeded jobs); and the two-subscriber identity test. Database-backed tests use the shared Postgres through FS3_TEST_DATABASE_URL — never start a container. If you need a dependency the daemon does not have (a streaming body helper, for example), STOP and ask the PM: dependency additions to fs3-daemon need an allowlist grant and the daemon's dependency list is deliberately short. |
